Dev Patel: Heads up: **Escalation Playbook v2** is now live ✅

This is the new source of truth for:
• severity + triage criteria (P0–P4 / Sev0–Sev3)
• Support + Eng/SRE SLAs by customer tier
• escalation paths + ownership map (who to page / when)
• customer comms templates (what to say / what *not* to promise)
• known-issues catalog + validated workarounds (internal + safe-to-share)

Confluence landing page: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/CSS/Escalation+Playbook+v2
Severity matrix + triage checklist: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/CSS/Severity+Matrix+and+Triage+Criteria
SLAs by tier: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/CSS/Support+and+Eng+SLAs+by+Tier
Ownership map: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/CSS/Escalation+Paths+and+Ownership+Map
Comms templates: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/CSS/Customer+Comms+Templates
Known issues index: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/CSS/Known+Issues+and+Workarounds

**Effective immediately** for new escalations. We’ll do a short “pilot + tune” window through the sprint (Feb–Mar) — please drop feedback in-thread.

Training sessions (30 min + 15 min Q&A):
1) Tue 2/25 10:00am PT / 1:00pm ET
2) Thu 2/27 3:00pm PT / 6:00pm ET
Calendar + deck: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RedwoodEscalationPlaybookV2

Big thanks to @Sean Gallagher @Elliot Price @Owen Phillips @Priya Shah + SRE/Docs/CS folks who cranked on this.

:rotating_light: **Reminder:** customer-identifying details for Private/enterprise need to stay in restricted systems (see playbook section “Restricted handling”).

Questions / edge cases welcome here.

— Dev

Jasmine Liu: +1. This should reduce the “who owns this?” churn we’ve been seeing. Please make sure CSMs are aligned on the tier-based comms expectations before promising timelines. If you need a quick sanity check on messaging, loop in CS.

Sean Gallagher: From SRE side: thank you for tightening the thresholds. The big change is **what counts as an incident vs support escalation** — please use the criteria in the handoff doc (linked from the landing page). If it’s not impacting multiple customers or a tier-1 service health issue, we want to keep it out of paging.

Elliot Price: Docs note: the Known Issues pages now have a **Safe-to-share** callout at the top. If it’s *not* marked safe-to-share, please don’t paste it into customer emails verbatim — use the comms templates + summarize.

Chris Osei: For reporting: starting next week we’ll track MTTA / time-to-mitigation on escalations using the new tags + required fields. If you see missing data, please nudge the ticket owner to fill it in (it’ll break the weekly rollup otherwise).

Owen Phillips: Support Eng heads up — the biggest win here is the **required fields** checklist. If you’re escalating without request IDs, env/region, model + approximate timestamps, it’s going to bounce back. This isn’t to be annoying; it’s because we lose hours every time.

Priya Shah: Known Issues sprint status: we published the first batch (streaming reconnects / 429s / Dedicated latency spikes). If you have a workaround you’ve been using that’s not documented, DM me or add it to the backlog tracker (link is on the index page).

Rafael Mendes: Oncall detail: if you do need to engage SRE, use the playbook’s “handoff to SRE” flow. The goal is to avoid a bunch of parallel pings. One escalation thread + one owner.

Miles Thornton: Incident-bot update is going out today — it’ll prompt for the new required fields and auto-drop the comms reminder. If it’s missing something you need, reply here and I’ll tune the form.

Rachel Kim: CS question I’ve been getting: for Dedicated customers, are we still doing after-hours investigation updates? (Some folks are used to “we’ll update every 30 mins no matter what” and that doesn’t seem sustainable.)

Dev Patel: @Rachel Kim yep — addressed in the SLA-by-tier table. Dedicated/Enterprise: we commit to *first response + cadence* based on severity, but we’re standardizing language so we don’t promise constant “meaningful updates” when nothing changed. The templates have the new phrasing (“next update by X even if no change”).

Sean Gallagher: Re after-hours: for Sev0/Sev1 we’ll do updates per the table, but please don’t invent an update interval in the moment. Use the matrix -> it maps to cadence.

Elliot Price: Also: we added a short “what not to say” section to the comms templates (e.g., don’t promise an RCA timeline until incident owner confirms). Worth a skim.

Owen Phillips: FYI we’ll run one of the training sessions as a scenario walk-through using real-ish examples (streaming disconnects + 429 spike). Bring your spicy edge cases.

Slackbot: Reminder: The training sessions start Tue 2/25 10:00am PT and Thu 2/27 3:00pm PT. Add to calendar here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RedwoodEscalationPlaybookV2

Dev Patel: Last thing: if you spot anything unclear/contradictory, comment directly on the Confluence page (or reply here) — we’ll incorporate edits before we lock “v2.1” at end of week 1.
